title: Deterministic binding matrix for model selectors across deployment channels
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Purpose: Define a deterministic, cross-environment resolution matrix for model selector pins (commit hashes, semver tags, and human tags) and publish stable performance profiles keyed to immutable identifiers. Goal is reproducible inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while keeping the SDK ergonomics simple for application engineers.

Scope: API + SDK surface for pin selectors, server-side resolution precedence, fallback behavior, rollout/rollback semantics, TTLs for mutable tags, and the policy for publishing performance profiles (latency/cost/SLOs) tied to immutable model versions. Does NOT include runtime kernel selection logic itself (handled by runtime team), but must expose enough metadata for routing decisions.

Background: Users can currently refer to models via several opaque strings (named tags, semver-like labels, commit sha). Observability and customer complaints show non-determinism when redirects/floating tags differ between regions or dedicated pools. This ticket formalizes resolution rules and the SDK shape so pinned consumers get predictable binding and cost/latency budgeting can be automated.

Key requirements:
- Resolution must be deterministic and idempotent for a given control-plane state snapshot. The same selector and control-plane snapshot must resolve to the same immutable model ref (commit hash) regardless of client environment.
- Provide clear precedence for overlapping selectors so client intent is unambiguous.
- Publish performance profiles (quantized latency, throughput, token costs) indexed by immutable commit SHA. Profiles for semver ranges or tags are derived aggregates but must reference the underlying SHAs used.
- SDK should surface a typed selector API and validate common user errors locally with helpful guidance.
- Support safe rollbacks: when an alias/tag is moved to a prior SHA, routing should be able to rollback without violating pinned clients' expectations when they explicitly pinned by immutable ref.
decisions: Canonical storage: store model artifacts and profiles by immutable commit SHA as the single source of truth.
Selector precedence: explicit immutable ref (commit) > exact semver (1.2.3) > semver range (^1.2.0, >=1.1 <2.0) > annotated release tag (e.g., release/rc) > floating alias 'latest'.

Profiles published at release time: performance profiles are attached to the commit SHA. Aggregated metrics for semver/tags are computed asynchronously and link back to the SHAs included in the aggregation.

SDK API: introduce Selector typed union strings and a small helper resolver API that returns resolved_sha, resolved_semver, and profile_ref. Example selector forms: 'sha:0a1b2c3d', 'semver:1.3.0', 'semver:^1.2.0', 'tag:stable-2025-02'.

Tag volatility policy: mutable tags must include a TTL/epoch metadata; if a tag is moved, publish an audit event and emit an advisory in the console. Client-side pins by tag will receive a warning recommending immutable pinning.

Fallback behavior: runtime may substitute a compatible quantized variant only if the client allows 'variant_fallback=true' in request. Otherwise return 409 conflict with the list of compatible SHAs and variants.
Backward compatibility: existing plain name selectors without prefix will be treated as 'tag:' for now, but SDK will deprecate this and emit lint warnings for unprefixed selectors.
tradeoffs: Strict immutability (commit-only pins) maximizes reproducibility but is less ergonomic for teams that want semantic version movement. We pick precedence to favor explicit immutability while preserving convenience via semver/tags.
Publishing profiles per SHA increases storage and compute cost for aggregation but gives precise cost/latency accounting per immutable artifact.
Adding SDK-side validation shifts some complexity to clients but prevents common operator errors that would otherwise require expensive rollback/investigation.
Allowing runtime variant substitution improves availability but introduces subtle behavioral differences; we gate it behind an explicit request flag to keep default behavior deterministic.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Drafted resolution matrix and initial SDK selector syntax. Shared with runtime and console teams for feedback.
2025-02-18: Spike completed comparing cost of storing per-SHA profiles vs. aggregated only. Prototype shows per-SHA profiles acceptable at current model churn rates.
2025-02-24: Convergence call with runtime, SDK, and console. Agreed on precedence and tag TTL concept. Action: design API wire format and API responses for resolver endpoint.

2025-03-01: PR created for SDK selectors and local validator (github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482). Riding tests: unit tests for selector parsing, integration tests to call control-plane resolver mock.
2025-03-04: Console UX design for pin warnings finished; design mock in Figma. Need PM sign-off on messaging for tag volatility.
comments: Marisol Ortega (2025-02-19): Request to include an explicit 'why' in SDK warnings — help users understand production risk of tag pins.
Ravi Patel (runtime) (2025-02-21): Suggested adding 'hardware compatibility' list in resolver response so routing can make safe choices for Dedicated pools.
Elena Ruiz (security) (2025-02-27): Asked for audit-event schema for tag moves and publish events for compliance. Adding small schema review to dependency list.
James Li (PM) (2025-03-02): Approved tag TTL defaults provided they can be overridden per-organization via admin settings.
acceptance_criteria: API: control-plane resolver endpoint returns resolved_sha, canonical_semver (if applicable), and profile_ref for a given selector and region.
SDK: new Selector type and parse/validate helpers released; unprefixed selectors emit deprecation warnings.
Console: UI surfaces tag volatility warnings and shows audit trail for tag moves.
Profiles: performance profile data ingested and queryable by SHA; aggregated semver/tag-level views reference the underlying SHAs.
Tests: end-to-end tests that pin by sha, semver range, and tag reproduce expected resolved SHA given a fixed control-plane snapshot fixture.
Docs: README and migration guide for customers to move from floating tags to immutable pins.
